edges.description: Loss of Adam9 in knockout mice disorganizes the apical processes of the retinal pigment epithelium.
Without normal apical microvilli, contact between the outer segments and the RPE apical surface is lost and the subretinal space widens.

Inferred link. The RPE changes seen on fundus examination in patients are taken to reflect the RPE pathology shown in the mouse and dog models; no study has examined ADAM9 patient RPE histologically to confirm it.
RPE cells extend elongated pseudopods across the enlarged subretinal space to ingest outer segment tips.
edges.target: Compensatory RPE Pseudopod Outer Segment Ingestion

edges.description: The POS-RPE junction anomaly precedes photoreceptor degeneration in knockout mice; the mechanism linking the two is not established, and the pseudopod work shows that the gap alone does not immediately impair photoreceptor function.

edges.target: Decreased rod and cone electroretinogram responses

edges.description: Vessel attenuation is a conventional secondary sign of advanced outer retinal degeneration; no ADAM9-specific study tests the link.
Disc pallor is a conventional secondary sign of advanced outer retinal degeneration; no ADAM9-specific study tests the link.
The RPE apical process defect is the earliest lesion in the knockout retina.
Rod and cone degeneration develops late in the knockout mouse.
edges.limitations: The mouse phenotype is milder and later than the human disease, and the mouse retina has no macula, so the macular, cone-dominant human presentation is not reproduced.
